0.zh: 札记页。108) 本页的特别目的

en: Of the inner condition of philosophy a general picture has been sketched in the treatise prefixed to the whole as an introduction; the outer condition, which does not belong before the critique, is therefore still not so uninteresting that notice of it might not quite properly be taken.

For not to mention the remarkable climatic differences which the consideration of it shows on the large scale as on the small, and even on the small surface of Germany, external appearances which have reference to philosophy are, already by their nature, more or less effects of inner relations and point back to these.

Circumstances and the dispensation of the time have in our days given philosophy a very extensive relation, and one not altogether unimportant for its inner culture, to a multitude of objects and people, who, if they could reflect on themselves, would themselves have to be astonished at how they came to it.

The general attention which philosophy has drawn upon itself has increased more and more the swarm of people who, since they cannot penetrate into it, at least buzz around it externally and make themselves useless by their humming.

A multitude of peaceful citizens of the scholars' state, who within the four posts of their bread-science have been contented people, has been startled out of its repose by the upheaval, or even revolution, threatened from the philosophical republic to all other sciences.

Certainly it is a remarkable sign of the time when even the curta supellex does not keep a Kurt Sprengel109) from taking notice of the transcendental philosophers, or when a solid, homespun understanding has to be heard from Tübingen: the time has not yet come when one could regard it as settled that the appearances of nature are determined by the laws of thought; or when an ill-bred young man from Lower Saxony, whom Röschlaub had chastised on account of his mendacity, must in the Int[elligenz-]Blatt of the Jen[aischen] A[llgemeinen] L[iteratur-]Z[eitung] rail against philosophy and against what this mob calls sophistry.

The frequently repeated scorn of belief in authority, of the lack of thinking for oneself, has finally had the consequence that anyone who is able to hunt up some triviality or other constitutes himself a philosopher made by his own hand, and when one gives him to understand that in face of Fichte, for example, he certainly has to be silent and in every way to lay his hand on his mouth, [he carries on] in the Int.-Blatt of the Allg.
Lit.-Zeit. quite unruly, insists on his independence, and is astonished not that the latter has made mention of him at all, but that he has said the true opinion about him.
zh: 关于哲学的内在状况，在那篇作为导论置于全书之前的文章里已经勾画出一幅总的图景；外在状况并不归批判管，但因此也并没有无趣到不可以对它作一番记述的地步。
因为，且不说对它的考察在大的方面和小的方面、甚至仅仅在德意志这块不大的地面上就显示出种种奇特的气候差异，那些与哲学有关的外在现象，按其本性就已经或多或少是内在关系的效果，并且回指这些内在关系。
时势与时代的安排在我们今天给哲学带来了一种极为广泛的、对它的内在教养并非完全不重要的关系，即与一大批对象和人物的关系；这些人要是能反省一下，自己一定会惊讶，他们究竟是怎么跟哲学扯上关系的。
哲学为自己引来的普遍关注，使那群人越来越大；他们既然钻不进哲学里去，至少就在外面围着它嗡嗡转，靠自己的嗡嗡声把自己弄得毫无用处。
学者国度里的一大群安分公民，本来在各自那门混饭吃的学问的四根桩子里面过得挺快活，却被哲学共和国向所有其他科学发出的震动甚至革命从安宁中惊扰起来。

这确实是一个奇特的时代征兆：连 curta supellex 也挡不住一位库尔特·施普伦格尔109)去注意先验哲学家；或者一种扎实而土气的知性不得不从图宾根那边发话：时代还没有到可以把自然现象由思维规律来决定这一点看成定论的时候；又或者一个从下萨克森来的没教养的年轻人——勒斯劳布曾因他爱撒谎而惩戒过他——非得在 Int[elligenz-]Blatt der Jen[aischen] A[llgemeinen] L[iteratur-]Z[eitung] 上痛骂哲学，痛骂这群群氓称之为诡辩的东西。
对权威信仰、对缺乏独立思考的反复蔑视，最终造成了这样的后果：谁只要能逮住随便什么琐屑之谈，就自己动手把自己立为哲学家；而要是有人让他明白，面对比如费希特，他无论如何都得闭嘴，无论如何都得用手捂住嘴，他就在 Allg. 的 Int.-Blatt 上
Lit.-Zeit. 表现得完全无法无天，硬要强调自己的独立性，而且他感到惊讶的，并不是费希特居然提到了他，而是费希特说出了关于他的真实看法。

en: All this and more forms a relation, wholly external to philosophy itself, to individual people; a far more extensive and more or less general relation to the entire public is formed by the busy activity of whole institutes, which, besides directing the course of literature as a whole and the welfare of all sciences, want in particular to look after and promote that of philosophy with the public.
Although the most justly famous of them, and the one most distinguished in the field of philosophical criticism through some masterworks brought to light in earlier times, the Jena General

Lit.-Zeit., could so little escape the common lot of human things that recently, with regard to philosophy, the proverb had almost come true of it: the pitcher goes to the water so long until it breaks, yet, after the wise and indeed praiseworthy maxim has been adopted by it, of refraining entirely from the review of more significant philosophical works, it does not fail to provide insignificant ones from time to time with a fitting sauce.

Partly in reviews, partly and especially in its own articles, the Upper-German Literary Gazette, otherwise also called the Salzburg one, provides the salad for it, which, because it is without salt and pepper, is seasoned with parsley by the Würzburg Learned Advertiser and, by the Tübingen one, is poured over with a gift of mild oil of harmless flatness, so that the public on the whole can at least still count on a kind of philosophical dish.

To these sheets, which, although they have gone out of fashion, still find a sale, there joins itself an accompanying institute under the name of a yearbook of literature, which, in the consciousness of its being an appendage, is, as is fair, modest, and on the whole recognizes and passes itself off merely as a mercantile advertisement office, but through a certain thoroughness even in philosophical judgements can still hold comparison with the out-of-fashion ones.

The Erlangen Literary Gazette has in the philosophical field raised itself through several reviews above the general noble simplicity and mediocrity, but has thereby come strongly into the repute of unlawfully favouring transcendental idealism and of generally attaching itself to the pernicious innovators, on which account also, quite briefly, in the Int.-Blatt of the Jena A. L. Z., against it, if the bell has not been rung, at least a little bell has been tinkled.
zh: 所有这一切以及更多的东西，构成了哲学本身与个别人之间一种完全外在的关系；而与整个公众之间一种广泛得多、或多或少普遍的关系，则是由整个机构的忙碌活动构成的，这些机构除了引导文学的总体进程和一切科学的福祉，还特别想在公众那里照管并促进哲学的福祉。
尽管它们当中那家理所当然最著名、并且凭早先公之于世的几部杰作而在哲学批判这一行里最为出色的，即《耶拿普通》
文学报》，它也那样逃不过人间事物的共同命运，以至于近来在哲学方面，那句谚语几乎在它身上成真了：罐子打水打得太久，终究要破；可是，既然它已经采纳了那条明智而且确实值得称赞的准则，即完全不去评论比较重要的哲学著作，它却仍然不缺本事，隔一阵子就给无足轻重的著作配上一道合口的浇汁。
那家上德意志的、平时又叫萨尔茨堡的《文学报》，一部分在书评里，一部分而且特别在自己的文章里，为它配上生菜；这生菜因为没有盐和胡椒，就被《维尔茨堡学者通报》撒上香芹，被《图宾根学者通报》浇上一份温和的油、一种无害的平淡，于是公众大体上至少还总能指望吃到一道哲学菜。
在这些虽然已经过气、却仍然有人买的报章旁边，又添上一家陪跑的机构，名字叫《文学年鉴》；它意识到自己只是陪跑的，所以照理也很谦虚，总体上只承认并自称是一家做生意的广告代办处，但凭某种彻底性，即使在哲学评论上，也还始终能跟那些过气的报章比一比。
《埃尔朗根文学报》在哲学这一行里凭好几篇书评超出了一般的、高贵的简单与平庸，但也因此落下一个很响的名声：说它不合法地偏袒先验观念论，总之是跟那些败事的革新者搅在一起；所以《耶拿普通文学报》的 Int.-Blatt 上也针对它简短地——即使没有敲大钟，至少也摇了一回铃。

en: However great and comprehensive the busyness of these institutes is, there are yet even individual people who seek to surpass them in industry in this respect, and among others a cooper110) distinguished by nature and diligence, who alone is capable of binding the whole great Heidelberg Tun of literature, which at every fair fills itself with such diverse ingredients, with a hoop worked out of one piece.

Infinitely agreeable must it be to a large part of the public, which, without demanding precisely exact and correct concepts, nevertheless desires a general Aperçu of each occasion's yield, and besides, through the instructive similes taken from animal-plants, duck-billed animals and from all three kingdoms of nature and art, attains a fairly complete knowledge of all the natural-historical and other curiosities of recent times, and, since there can never be enough gossip in civil life anyway, is here moreover regaled with town gossip from the learned world.

Since in Germany everything is imitated, it is to be feared that, just as according to the above remark philosophy and each individual branch of literature, but especially of industry, draws its swarm of insects after it, so a peculiar species of big fat blowflies might form, which settle not merely on individual products but on the whole of literature.
One such fly has recently, probably unnoticed by the editors, settled in the Stuttg.
Allg.

Zeitung111) fair report, and indeed on Hegel's writing Difference of the Fichtean and Schellingian Systems of Philosophy, and we draw attention to it all the more since this is precisely an example of what credible gossip and well-grounded news of the matter the public has to expect in this way.112)
zh: 这些机构的忙碌无论多么大、多么广，却甚至有单个人想在这件事上靠勤勉超过它们，其中就有一位凭天性和勤奋而杰出的箍桶匠110)，只有他一个人有本事把文学这只整只的海德堡大酒桶——它每逢集市就装上各式各样五花八门的配料——用一道整块打出来的箍给箍上。
公众中很大一部分人一定觉得无比惬意：他们并不要求精确而正确的概念，却还是想要对每一次的收获有一个总的 Aperçu；此外还借那些有教益的比喻——它们取自动物植物、鸭嘴兽以及自然和艺术的所有三个王国——获得对近来一切自然史奇闻和其他奇闻差不多完整的知识；又因为市民生活里的闲谈本来就嫌不够，在这里还可以额外享用来自学术界的小道消息。
既然在德意志什么都被仿效，那就令人担心：正如按上面所说，哲学以及文学的每一单个门类、尤其是工业的每一单个门类都招来自己的虫群，说不定也会生出一种又大又肥的绿头苍蝇，它们不只落在个别产品上，而是落在整个文学上。
这样一只苍蝇不久前还——多半没被编者察觉——落到 Stuttg.
Allg.
Zeitung111) 的集市报道上，而且还落到黑格尔那篇《费希特与谢林哲学体系的差别》上；我们越发要提请大家注意它，因为这恰好是一个例子，说明公众走这条路可以指望得到什么样可信的闲话和真有实事根据的消息。112)

en: All this that we have adduced here, although it is only a few traits of it, we count as belonging to the external condition of the sciences.
What of this relates to philosophy we shall touch upon in this notes sheet, in the hope of recommending it to our readers, especially through attention to the German reviewing system.

For to whom will it not be agreeable to find here specially preserved the excellent utterances and philosophical sentiments which lie hidden as single pearls among the mass of other reviews and in the voluminous tomes of the learned sheets; whom will it not interest if we, concluding from these utterances, can give the curious public information and notice of the own fundamental propositions of many a judge and of their philosophical systems, which without our effort would probably remain hidden forever, since, as is well known, the philosophical reviewers at critical institutes, with the exception of the Erlangen Literary Gazette, in which, it is said, otherwise well-known philosophical writers too, such as Fichte, Steffens, Eschenmayer, Schelling and others, have taken part with contributions, are as a rule simply not in the habit of occupying themselves with the writing and composing of their own writings or even with the setting up of fundamental propositions and systems.
zh: 我们这里所列举的这一切——尽管它只是其中几个特征——我们都算作科学的外在状况。
其中与哲学有关的部分，我们将在本札记页上谈到，希望尤其借着对德意志书评事业的关注，把它推荐给我们的读者。

因为，谁不会乐于看到那些出色的说法和哲学情感——它们藏在大量别的书评里、藏在学者报章的那些厚卷里，像一颗颗单独的珍珠——在这里被特别保存下来呢；又有谁不会感兴趣，如果我们从这些说法出发推断，能够把某些评论者自己的根本命题和他们的哲学体系告知并通报给好奇的公众，而这些命题和体系要是没有我们这番努力，多半会永远隐藏着；因为众所周知，各批判机构里的哲学评论家——除了《埃尔朗根文学报》，据说连费希特、施特芬斯、埃申迈尔、谢林等本来就有名的哲学作家都给它投过稿——照例恰恰不习惯去写和撰自己的著作，更不用说提出根本命题和体系了。

5.en: The Relation of Scepticism to Philosophy. Presentation of Its Various Modifications and Comparison of the Newest with the Old113)
5.zh: 怀疑论与哲学的关系。对其各种变体的阐述以及最新近者与古代者的比较113)

en: Critique of Theoretical Philosophy by Gottlob Ernst Schulze, Court Counsellor and Professor in Helmstedt.
Hamburg, at C. E. Bohn, 1801.
Vol. 1, 728 pp., preface
XXXII pp.; vol. 2, 722 pp., preface
VI pp.
zh: 戈特洛布·恩斯特·舒尔策《理论哲学批判》，宫廷顾问、赫尔姆施泰特教授。
汉堡，C. E. Bohn 出版社，1801 年。
第 1 卷 728 S.，序言
XXXII S.；第 2 卷 722 S.，序言
VI S.

en: Eight years after Herr Schulze had come forward with a stir against the Kantian philosophy, chiefly in the form that it had acquired in the Theory of the Faculty of Representation114), he now embraces theoretical philosophy in general, in order to set it ablaze through his scepticism and to burn it down to its very foundation.

The whole brilliant crowd of the new sceptics rightly reveres Herr Schulze as its leader, and this sandbag of — for the present four alphabet-books — which Herr Schulze has dragged up against the fortress of philosophy rightly secures him this first place.
zh: 八年前，舒尔策先生曾以引起轰动的姿态出场，反对康德哲学，尤其是它在《表象能力理论》中获得的那种形态114)，如今他却把理论哲学整个儿都揽了过来，要用自己的怀疑论把它点燃，一直烧到地基。
新怀疑论者这整整一伙聪明人，理所当然地尊舒尔策先生为首领，而舒尔策先生拖到哲学要塞跟前来的这只沙袋——眼下是四本识字课本——也理所当然地为他保住了这第一把交椅。

en: The presentation and appraisal of this newest scepticism makes it necessary for us to enter into the relation of this scepticism, as well as of scepticism in general, to philosophy; by this relation the various modifications of scepticism will determine themselves of their own accord, and at the same time the relation of this newest scepticism itself, which supposes it has stood upon the shoulders of the old one and imagines that it both sees further and doubts more reasonably, to the old one will emerge.

An exposition of the relation of scepticism to philosophy, and a cognition of scepticism itself arising from it, seems not without merit also for the reason that the concepts commonly to be found about it are highly formal, and that its noble essence, when it is genuine, is wont to be turned into a general hiding-place and an excuse for unphilosophy in the most recent times.
zh: 要描述和评估这种最新的怀疑论，我们就不得不去弄清这种怀疑论、以及一般怀疑论与哲学的关系；依照这一关系，怀疑论的各种变样会自行确定下来，同时这种最新怀疑论本身与旧怀疑论的关系也会随之得出——它自以为站到了旧怀疑论的肩膀上，既看得更远，又怀疑得更合理。
讨论怀疑论与哲学的关系，并由此获得对怀疑论本身的认识，看来也并非没有功劳，因为通常关于它所能找到的那些概念极其形式化，而它一旦是真的，它那高贵的本质就往往被倒转为近来不搞哲学的人通用的藏身洞和托词。

en: Of the subjective source of Schulze's scepticism the introduction gives us a story; it contains the carrying out of the thought: if a cognition that is to be drawn from reason could obtain no general and lasting approval, if its workers stand in constant contradiction with one another and every new attempt to confer on this cognition the solidity of a science fails, then one may infer from this with fair certainty that the search for such a cognition must rest on an unattainable final end and on an illusion common to all its workers; also on the author's way of thinking about philosophy — as no one is to be blamed for a general distrust of the high praises of the insight and wisdom of reason — the observation of the success that the striving of so many men, venerable through their talents and through the zeal they showed in the search for hidden truths, has always had after a scientific philosophy, has had a strong influence, and has given it that direction out of which this critique of theoretical philosophy has arisen.

Every inclination to employ his powers on the working out of one of these systems, which just seemed to him to contain the surest indication of truth and certainty, was again and again suppressed, as soon as he made arrangements to satisfy it, quite especially by the consideration of the fate that has befallen all speculative occupation with the ultimate grounds of our cognition of the existence of things; for his confidence in his abilities did not go so far that he could entertain the hope of really attaining that after which so many men furnished with the greatest talents and the most manifold insights had striven in vain.
zh: 关于舒尔策式怀疑论的主观来源，导论给了我们一段故事；其中发挥的是这样一个想法：如果一种应当从理性中汲取来的认识不能为自己赢得普遍而持久的赞同，如果这种认识的加工者彼此一直处于矛盾之中，如果每一次要给这种认识赋予科学之坚固性的新尝试都失败，那么由此便相当可靠地推断出：对这种认识的寻求，必定以某个达不到的终极目的和一种为所有加工者共有的迷误为根据；此外，观察自古以来那么多凭其才能、凭其在寻找隐藏真理时所表现的热忱而令人尊敬的人追求一门科学哲学取得了怎样的成效，对作者先生关于哲学的想法——人们对理性之洞见和智慧所受到的高声赞美普遍心存怀疑，这谁也怪不得——也产生了强烈的影响，并给了它那样一个方向，这种理论哲学的批判就是从那个方向产生的。
每当他想去满足这种偏好时，那种要把力气用在这些体系之一的加工上的倾向——那个体系在他看来说的正好是最可靠地指向真理和确定性——就一次又一次被压了下去，尤其是通过对命运的这一考虑：一切就我们对事物存在的认识的最后根据所作的思辨活动，遭遇的都是这种命运；因为他对自己的才能并没有信任到能够抱有这样的希望：现实地达到那么多具有最大才能、最丰富洞见的人徒然追求过的东西。

en: That is truly spoken to the people's mouth and out of the people's mouth. - The Athenian lawgiver had set death upon political apragmosyne at the time when unrest should break out in the state; the philosophical apragmosyne, of taking no party for oneself but being resolved beforehand to submit to whatever fate crowns with victory and universality, is afflicted in itself with the death of speculative reason.

If indeed the consideration of fate could become a moment in the esteem and adoption of a philosophy, then it would not be universality but on the contrary non-universality that would have to be a moment of recommendation, since it is intelligible that the most genuine philosophies are not those which become universal, and that, if in addition to bad philosophies obtaining a universality, more genuine ones also attain it, the side of them that has become universal is precisely that which is not philosophical, so that even in these philosophies, which enjoy a so-called happier fate — which, however, in truth, if here there can be talk of happy or unhappy fate at all, is to be regarded as a misfortune — the non-universal would have to be sought out in order to find the philosophy. - If, however, Herr Schulze has seen that the success of the striving of so many men venerable through talents and zeal in the occupation with the investigation of the ultimate grounds of our cognition has been equally unhappy, this can count only as a highly subjective way of seeing; Leibniz, e.g., expresses a quite different way of seeing in the passage that Jacobi made one of his mottos: "J'ai trouvé que la plupart des sectes ont raison dans une bonne partie de ce qu'elles avancent, mais non pas tant en ce qu'elles nient."116) The superficial view of philosophical disputes lets one glimpse only the differences of the systems, but already the old rule "contra negantes principia non est disputandum" makes it known that when philosophical systems dispute with one another — it is of course another matter when philosophy disputes with unphilosophy — unity in the principles is present, which, exalted above all success and fate, cannot be recognized from that about which the dispute is carried on, and escapes the gaping gaze that always glimpses the opposite of what goes on before its eyes.

With the principles, or with reason, all those men venerable through talents and zeal have indeed succeeded, and the difference is to be placed solely in the higher or lower abstraction through which reason has presented itself in principles and systems.

Not presupposing the failure of speculative truth, modesty and the hopelessness of attaining what only the superficial view persuades itself the venerable men failed to attain fall away; or else, presupposing that failure, there is no question, if modesty and distrust of one's abilities could provide the other moment alongside that of the consideration of success, which modesty is the greater — not to entertain the hope of attaining that after which the men full of talent and insight had striven in vain, or else, as Herr Schulze says happened to him, to hit upon the conjecture that some hereditary defect clings to philosophy and must have propagated itself from a dogmatic occupation with it (we shall see later that Herr Schulze knows only sceptical and dogmatic philosophizing) to the other.

That Herr Schulze trusts himself to have discovered this hereditary defect and sets forth what he has discovered of it in the present work proves that he thinks as little of the moment of modesty in philosophy, although he speaks of it, as is to be thought of it as well as of the moment of success.
zh: 这真是投民众之所好，而且是从民众嘴里说出来的话。——对于政治上的不作为（Apragmosyne），即在国家发生动乱之时的不作为，雅典的立法者规定处以死刑；而哲学上的不作为，即自己不去站到哪一边，而是事先就决心屈服于命运以胜利和普遍性加冕的那一方，它本身就得上了思辨理性之死。

如果对命运的考虑真的能成为敬重和采纳一种哲学的一个环节，那么成为推荐理由的环节就不该是普遍性，恰恰相反，应当是非普遍性，因为可以理解，最真实的哲学并不是那些变得普遍的哲学，而且，如果说坏哲学获得了普遍性、更真实的哲学也达到了普遍性，那么它们身上变得普遍的那一面恰恰就是非哲学的东西，所以即使在那些享有所谓较幸运的命运的哲学那里——这种命运其实在这里根本谈得上幸运或不幸命运的时候，只能算作不幸——也必须去找出非普遍的东西，才能找到哲学。——不过，如果舒尔策先生看到，那么多凭才能和热忱而令人尊敬的人在研究我们认识的最后根据这件事上，追求的结果同样是不幸的，那么这只算是一种极其主观的看法。例如莱布尼茨就在雅可比用作自己一条题词的那段话里表达了一种完全不同的看法："J'ai trouvé que la plupart des sectes ont raison dans une bonne partie de ce qu'elles avancent, mais non pas tant en ce qu'elles nient."116)。对哲学争执的肤浅看法只让人看到各体系之间的差别，但古老的规则 "contra negantes principia non est disputandum" 已经表明，当哲学体系互相争执时——当然，哲学与非哲学争执时是另一回事——诸原则中是存在一致的，这种一致超乎一切成效和命运之上，不能从争执所争的东西里认出来，也躲开了那种呆看，这种呆看看到的总是眼前所发生之事的反面。
就原则、或者说就理性而言，那些凭才能和热忱而令人尊敬的人其实都成功了，差别只在于抽象的高低，理性正是以这种抽象在诸原则和诸体系中把自己呈现出来。

如果不预先设定思辨真理的失败，那么谦逊以及达到下面这种东西的无望就都消失了，而只有肤浅的看法才使自己相信那些令人尊敬的人没有达到这种东西；或者反过来，如果预先设定那种失败，那么只要谦逊和对自身才能的不信任能充当与成效之考虑并列的另一个环节，问题就只在于哪种谦逊更大——是不去抱有达到那些有才能、有洞见的人徒然追求过的东西的希望，还是像舒尔策先生说的发生在他身上的那样，竟猜想到哲学身上附着某种遗传缺陷，并且它必定从对哲学的一种独断的从事（我们后面会看到，舒尔策先生只知道怀疑式的和独断式的哲学活动）传染到了另一种从事上去。
舒尔策先生自认为发现了这种遗传缺陷，并把他在其中发现的东西写进了眼前这部著作，这就证明，他尽管口头上谈哲学中谦逊这一环节，却对它同样不看重，正如对它以及对成效这一环节本就不该看重一样。

en: The discovery of the hereditary defect of all previous speculative philosophy is thus promised in this work; and by this discovery, which concerns previous philosophy, says Schulze, 1st part S. 610, all hope of a success of speculation is also cut off for the future, because it would be foolish (indeed!) to hope for a change in the human cognitive powers.

But what happier discovery than this one of a hereditary defect of all speculation can be brought to the people fond of philosophy, which either always justifies its removal from speculating, which after all needs no justification, by the dispute of philosophy, and gives itself out as inclined to surrender to a system if only a philosophical council or colloquy on a universally valid philosophy would once agree, — or which itself runs after all philosophical systems (and counts every thought-mushroom among them), but whose intellectual chemistry is so unhappily organized as to have an affinity only for the alloy mixed into the nobler metal of a coin and to precipitate itself with this alone, and which again and again becomes aware that it has only been fooled, and finally in despair throws itself into the moral, yet still with anxieties from the speculative side, — what happier discovery can be made for these two parts than that speculative philosophy itself lacks [it] in its innermost essence?

To the first, the proof is given that he was the cleverest, since he thought nothing of speculative philosophy; the latter, for having always been fooled, is consoled by the guilt being rolled off him and onto philosophy and his anxieties about speculative philosophy being taken from him.

It is therefore no wonder if this scepticism obtains, if not general, yet widespread approval, and if especially over the present ponderous treatment of it such a joy arises, of which our Notizenblatt117) contains an example.
zh: 因此，这部著作许诺的是发现迄今为止一切思辨哲学的遗传缺陷；舒尔策说（第 1 部分 S. 610），通过这一涉及以往哲学的发现，思辨在未来取得成功的全部希望也被一刀切断，因为指望人类认识能力发生变化是愚蠢的（说得对！）。

对于爱好哲学的民众，还能献上什么比这更幸运的发现，即发现一切思辨都有遗传缺陷——这种民众要么总是拿哲学的争执来为自己远离思辨作辩解（远离思辨本来根本不需要辩解），并声称只要有一次关于一种普遍有效的哲学的哲学会议或座谈能达成一致，它就愿意归附某个体系；——要么它自己追逐一切哲学体系（它把每一个思想的蘑菇都算在里面），可它的智性化学组织得如此不幸，只对掺进硬币那较贵重金属里的合金有亲和力，并且只跟这合金一起沉淀下来，于是它一再发觉自己只是被耍了，最后绝望地一头扎进道德里去，却又仍带着从思辨方面来的担忧；——对这两部分人，还能做出什么比这更幸运的发现，就是发现思辨哲学在最内在的本质里本身就有所欠缺？
前一种人得到了证明：他是最聪明的，因为他根本不看重思辨哲学；后一种人则因为老是被耍而得到安慰：罪责从他身上被推到了哲学身上，他对思辨哲学的担忧也被拿掉了。
所以，这种怀疑论即使没有赢得普遍的赞同，也赢得了广泛的赞同，而且尤其是对眼前这部笨重的怀疑论著作产生了那样一种喜悦——我们的 Notizenblatt117) 就载有一个例子——这都不足为奇。

en: Herr Schulze excludes the practical and the aesthetic part from his sceptical treatment of philosophy and limits it to theoretical philosophy. - Judging by everything, it seems that Herr Schulze holds theoretical philosophy alone to be speculative philosophy, but the remaining parts of it for one knows not what; or rather, one nowhere catches a trace of the idea of a speculative philosophy that is neither particularly theoretical, nor practical, nor aesthetic.

To that division of philosophy, moreover, Herr Schulze arrives through empirical psychology, although he himself excludes the same from philosophy, but strangely enough still uses it as the source of a division of philosophy; namely, important differences are supposed to occur on the facts of consciousness, they are either cognitions of objects or expressions of the will or feelings of pleasure and displeasure, to which the feelings of the beautiful and the sublime also belong; they cannot, so far as our insight into them reaches, be reduced to a single class or derived from a single source (words that we read verbatim in Kant, Critique of the Power of Judgement, Introduction

S. XXII), but are essentially different from one another through lasting marks and give the three parts of philosophy named above. - Already in this Herr Schulze differs essentially from Sextus Empiricus118), who in his critique of the individual parts of philosophy and of the sciences does not himself make the division, but takes it as he finds it and attacks it sceptically.
zh: 舒尔策先生把实践部分和审美部分从他的怀疑论哲学处理中排除出去，把它限制在理论哲学上。——从各方面看，舒尔策先生似乎把理论哲学单独当作思辨哲学，而哲学的其余部分则被当作谁也不知道的什么东西；或者不如说，到处都看不到一丝关于一种既不是特殊的理论哲学、也不是实践哲学、也不是审美哲学的思辨哲学的观念的痕迹。
舒尔策先生之达到哲学的那种划分，靠的是经验心理学，尽管他自己把经验心理学排除在哲学之外，却又够奇怪地把它当作哲学划分的来源来用；也就是说，在意识的事实上应当出现重要的区别：它们要么是对客体的认识，要么是意志的表现，要么是愉快和不快的情感，美感和崇高感也属于后者；而按我们对它们的洞见所及，它们不能被归结为一个唯一的类，也不能从一个唯一的来源推导出来（这些话我们逐字读于康德《判断力批判》导论
S. XXII），而是通过持久的标志本质上彼此有别，并且给出上面提到的哲学的三个部分。——仅此一点，舒尔策先生就已经与塞克斯都·恩披里柯118) 根本不同：后者在他对哲学和科学的各个部分的批判中，自己并不作出这种划分，而是照他发现的样子把它拿过来，并对它作怀疑论的攻击。

en: Before all things we have to see how Herr Schulze conceives this theoretical philosophy and how the enemy he strikes to the ground is actually constituted.

In the first section, in a highly methodical manner running through several pages, the essential marks of theoretical philosophy are sought out and the following definition is brought out: theoretical philosophy is the science of the supreme and most unconditioned causes of everything conditioned, of whose actuality we otherwise have certainty. - This other certainty of the conditioned without philosophy we shall come to know later.

But the supreme and unconditioned causes themselves, or better, the rational, Herr Schulze again conceives as things that lie beyond our consciousness, something existent, absolutely opposed to consciousness; of rational cognition there never occurs any representation other than the one repeated to nausea, that through it a cognition of things is to be acquired which are supposed to lie hidden behind the silhouettes of things that the natural mode of cognition of human beings holds before us; with the help of abstract fundamental propositions and concepts determinate being is to be found out, it is to be scouted out what things, taken in their true and hidden actuality, are supposed to be; the tool that philosophy employs for its scouting out of things is said to be concepts, abstract fundamental propositions, inferences from concepts, and the bridge to those hidden things is again built out of nothing but concepts. - It is not possible to conceive the rational and speculation in a cruder way; speculative philosophy is constantly represented as if before it common experience in the immovable form of its common actuality lay spread out invincibly as its iron horizon, and as if behind this horizon it suspected and wanted to seek out the things in themselves of its horizon as a mountain range of an equally common actuality that carries that other actuality on its shoulders; the rational, the in-itself, Herr Schulze can represent to himself in no other way than as a rock under snow; for the Catholic the host changes into a divine-living thing; here what the devil demanded of Christ, to change stone into bread, does not happen, but the living bread of reason changes eternally into stone.
zh: 首先我们要看看，舒尔策先生是如何理解这种理论哲学的，以及他打倒在地的那个敌人究竟是什么样子。
在第一节里，作者以极其讲究方法、贯穿好几页的方式寻找理论哲学的本质标志，并得出下面这个定义：理论哲学是关于一切受条件限制者的最高、最无条件的原因的科学，而这些受条件限制者的现实性我们本来是有确定性的。——这种不靠哲学而关于受条件限制者的本来确定性，我们后面会认识到。

但那些最高、无条件的原因本身，或者不如说理性的东西，舒尔策先生又一概理解为超出我们意识之外的物，某种存在着的、与意识绝对对立的东西；关于理性的认识，出现的不外乎那种令人作呕地一再重复的表象：靠它可以获得对事物的认识，而这些事物据说隐藏在人的自然认识方式所摆在我们面前的事物的剪影后面；借助抽象的根本命题和概念，应当把定在找出来，应当侦察出事物在真正而隐蔽的现实性中究竟是什么；哲学用来侦察事物的工具，据说是概念、抽象的根本命题、从概念得出的推论，而通往那些隐蔽事物的桥又是用无非概念的东西搭起来的。——不可能比这更粗陋地理解理性的东西和思辨了；思辨哲学一直被说成是这样：仿佛在它面前，普通经验以其普通现实性那不可移动的形式不可逾越地铺展开来，作为它铁一般的视野，而它在这视野后面猜测并要去寻找视野内的事物本身，把它们当作同样普通的现实性的一座山脉，这座山脉肩上扛着那另一种现实性；理性的东西、自在的东西，舒尔策先生根本无法把它想象成别的东西，只能想象成雪下的一块石头；在天主教徒那里，圣饼变成神圣而有生命的东西；这里发生的不是魔鬼向基督要求的事——把石头变成面包，而是理性的活面包永远变成石头。

en: To this speculative philosophy, which attempts a cognition of things that are supposed to exist outside our consciousness, the positive side of this scepticism stands opposed; for it does not merely have the negative side, which occupies itself with destroying the fantasies of the dogmatists and their attempts to attain cognitions of the existence of hyperphysical things.
zh: 与这种思辨哲学——它试图去认识那些据说存在于我们意识之外的事物——相对立的，是这种怀疑论的肯定方面；因为它不只有否定方面，即致力于摧毁独断论者的胡思乱想以及他们为获得关于超物理事物存在的认识所作的努力。

en: The positive side of this scepticism consists namely in this, that it is generally described as a philosophy that does not go beyond consciousness, and indeed (S. 51) the existence of that which is given within the compass of our consciousness has undeniable certainty; for since it is present in consciousness, we can doubt its certainty as little as consciousness itself; but to want to doubt consciousness is absolutely impossible, because such a doubt, since it cannot take place without consciousness, would annihilate itself, and hence would be nothing.

What is given in and with consciousness one calls a fact of consciousness, and consequently the facts of consciousness are the undeniable actual, to which all philosophical speculations must relate and which is to be explained or made intelligible by these speculations.
zh: 这种怀疑论的肯定方面就在于：它一般被描述为一种不超出意识的哲学，而且（S. 51）在意识范围内被给予的东西的存在具有不可否认的确定性；因为既然它在意识中是当前在场的，我们就既不能怀疑它的确定性，也不能怀疑意识本身；而要想怀疑意识，则是绝对不可能的，因为这样一种怀疑既然没有意识就不能成立，它就会毁灭自身，因而什么也不是。
在意识中并与意识一起被给予的东西，人们称之为意识的事实，因此意识的事实就是不可否认的现实东西，一切哲学思辨都必须与它相关，并且要由这些思辨来加以解释或使之可以理解。

en: To this philosophy, which places undeniable certainty in the facts of consciousness and, exactly like the most ordinary Kantianism, restricts all rational cognition (S. 21) to the formal unity that is to be brought into those facts, the question cannot be put how it then conceives that the human being does not satisfy himself with this undeniable certainty that he finds in the eternal staring perception of objects, how it then also means to conceive that ordering of perceptions out of this perceiving? how the human being goes beyond the bestiality of such an existence, which, to speak with Herr Schulze, consists in the perceiving of the real being of things, and comes to a thought of what Herr Schulze calls metaphysics, of a tracing of that real being to its grounds or a derivation of this real being and everything that belongs to it from a primal ground, in order to make it intelligible? - This facts-philosophy has no other than the dull answer that that striving after a cognition which lies beyond the real, wholly certain being of things, thus recognizing it as uncertain, is also a fact of consciousness; Herr Schulze says this (1st part, S. 21) thus: by virtue of an original arrangement of our mind we have namely a longing, for everything that according to our insight exists only conditionally, to seek out the last and unconditioned ground.

But if every fact of consciousness has immediate certainty, then an insight that something exists only conditionally is impossible; for to exist conditionally and to be nothing certain for oneself are synonymous. - The author expresses himself similarly S. 72, when he makes the transition from that bestial staring at the world and its undeniable certainty to the problem of theoretical philosophy: although the being of things, according to the pronouncements of consciousness, is wholly certain, this by no means satisfies reason (here we shall learn what it consists in), because with existing things that we know it does not follow of itself that they are and that they are what they are.

The intuiting subject cognizes the objects and their existence immediately, absolutely, and as something that subsists and is for itself in as perfect a manner independently of the effects of the power of representation as the cognizing subject subsists and is for itself. - How, with this absolute certainty that and how things exist, is it at the same time not to be understood of itself that they are and that they are what they are?

There is at the same time asserted a cognition according to which the existence and constitution of things is self-evident, and another according to which this existence and constitution is not at all self-evident.

No more complete contradiction can be devised between the preceding and this manner of making the search for a rational cognition intelligible, and no more oblique and pinched transition to metaphysics.
zh: 对这种哲学——它把不可否认的确定性放进意识的事实，并且完全像最平庸的康德主义那样，把一切理性认识（S. 21）限制在应当带进那些事实里去的形式统一性上——不能提出这样的问题：它怎么竟能以概念把握，人凭着他在对客体永恒呆滞的知觉中找到的这种不可否认的确定性并不满足，它又怎么竟想从这种知觉出发去以概念把握那种对知觉的整理？人怎么竟会超出这样一种存在的兽性——用舒尔策先生的话说，这种存在就在于知觉事物的实在存在——并达到关于舒尔策先生称之为形而上学的东西的思想，即对那种实在存在加以追究，或者把这种实在存在以及属于它的一切从一个原始根据推导出来，以便使它变得可以理解？——这种事实哲学只有一种迟钝的回答：那种超出事物的实在而完全确定的存在的认识追求，因而也就是把这种认识认作不确定的追求，同样也是意识的一个事实；舒尔策先生（第 1 部分 S. 21）是这样说的：凭借我们心情的一种原初安排，我们对一切按我们的洞见只是有条件地存在的东西，都有一种要找出其最后而无条件的根据的渴望。

但如果每一个意识的事实都具有直接的确定性，那么"某物只是有条件地存在"这一洞见就是不可能的；因为有条件地存在和自在地不是任何确定的东西，是同一个意思。——作者在 S. 72 也是这样表述的，当他把那种对世界的兽性呆视及其不可否认的确定性过渡到理论哲学的问题时说道：尽管按照意识的各种说法，事物的存在是完全确定的，但这根本不使理性满足（这里我们将认识到理性究竟是什么），因为对于我们所认识的现存事物来说，它们存在、并且它们就是它们所是的那个东西，并不是不言自明的。
直观着的主体直接地、无条件地认识对象及其存在，并且把它们认识为这样一种东西：它同认识着的主体自为地存在和是的那样，以同样完满的方式不依赖于表象力的作用而自为地存在和是。——在事物存在以及如何存在具有这种绝对确定性的情况下，怎么同时又会不是不言自明地知道：它们存在，并且它们就是它们所是的那个东西？
人们同时主张一种认识，按这种认识，事物的存在和性状是不言自明的；又主张另一种认识，按这种认识，这种存在和性状根本不是不言自明的。
在前面的说法与这种把寻求理性认识说得可以理解的方式之间，想不出比这更完全的矛盾；也想不出比这更歪斜、更别扭的向形而上学的过渡。

en: After we have illuminated the positive side of this scepticism, we pass over to its negative side, to which the whole third part of the first volume is devoted.

Herr Schulze himself feels that a scepticism that ascribes an undeniable certainty to the facts of consciousness agrees but little with the concept of scepticism that the ancient sceptics give us; we have first to hear Herr Schulze's own opinion about this difference.
He explains himself about it in the introduction and the first section of the third part.

In the first place he reminds us that it has indeed often been the case that the one who first found a thought on the path of truth understood far less of its content, its grounds and its consequences than others who after him carefully investigated its origin and its meaning; hitherto the true intention of scepticism has for the most part been misjudged, and so on. The scepticism that Herr Schulze regards as the true one and as a more perfect one than that of the ancients relates, namely, to the judgements peculiar to philosophy, i.e. those which, as Herr Schulze expresses the final aim of this science, determine the absolute or at least supersensible, i.e. the grounds, existing outside the sphere of consciousness, of the something that, according to the testimonies of our consciousness, exists in a conditioned way.

The judgements that belong only to philosophy, however, are said to be no object of this scepticism; for they either express so-called facts of consciousness or are grounded on analytical thinking; their truth can therefore, even according to scepticism, be fathomed and seen; by contrast, it asserts against theoretical philosophy that about the grounds, existing outside the scope of our consciousness or, as the author also says, not given in it as to their existence, of the being of things, or about the things that exist besides the existing things, nothing at all can be known.

Herr Schulze himself has the objection made against this concept of scepticism, that according to it nothing of what experience teaches, and in particular not the aggregate of outer sensations, and also of all sciences only philosophy (since no other has to do with the cognition of things outside the scope of consciousness) could be an object of sceptical doubt, whereas the old scepticism extended to both and the oldest at least to the former.

On this point Herr Schulze chiefly cites that the beginning and course of scepticism has always determined itself according to the presumptions of the dogmatists; the ancient sceptics admit that there is a cognition through the senses and a conviction through it of the determinate being and certain properties of things subsisting for themselves, according to which every rational human being has to direct himself in active life. - In this, that such a conviction was directed merely to active life, it lies immediately that it had nothing to do with philosophy, that it and the limited consciousness, filled with facts, was by no means set over against reason and philosophy as a principle of an undeniable certainty, and least of all set up in a boasting manner against them, but was only the tribute, arranged as narrowly as possible, that was paid to the necessity of an objective determining; we would not, say the sceptics, choose this or avoid that when it concerns things that lie in our power, but those things which are not in our power but are according to necessity we cannot avoid, such as being hungry, thirsty, cold; for these cannot be cleared out of the way by reason.

But the consciousness that is connected with these necessary needs - the ancient sceptic was far from elevating it to the rank of a knowledge that is an objective assertion; paying attention to what appears, we live, says Sextus119), because we cannot be entirely inactive, according to common life-understanding, without thereby making any opinion or assertion.

But of a conviction about things and their properties there is no talk in this scepticism; the criterion of scepticism, Sextus expresses himself, is what appears (ϕαινόμενον), by which we in fact understand its appearance (ϕαντασίαν αὐτου ͂), thus the subjective; for since it lies in conviction (πείσει, but not of a thing) and in an involuntary being-affected, no investigation takes place; it is ἀζήτητος (the German expression "doubt", used of scepticism, is always askew and unsuitable).

But that the sceptics declared all perception, instead of ascribing undeniable certainty to it, to be mere illusion, and asserted that one must just as well state the opposite of what one has stated of the object according to its appearance, just as well say that honey is bitter as that it is sweet, - that, as Herr Schulze himself cites, the first ten and proper tropes of the sceptics concerned solely this insecurity of sense perception, for that Herr Schulze gives the reason that sensations were already in the earliest times of speculative philosophy passed off by the dogmatists as an appearance, though something entirely different lies at its ground, and that a correspondence was ascribed to the appearance itself with that which is supposed to be situated behind it as the proper thing, indeed that cognition through sensations was even many times asserted by them as a science of the object lying hidden behind the sensation.

For this reason the sceptics attacked these doctrines of the dogmatists concerning the certainty of sensory cognition and denied that by means of the object in sensation anything can be reliably cognized of that which is supposed to be situated behind this object as the true and proper thing subsisting for itself. - Here, with regard to the ancient philosophers, there is expressed exactly the same crudest representation that Herr Schulze has of rational cognition; but the interpretation as if the scepticism had attacked not the sensory perceptions themselves but only the things placed behind and beneath them by the dogmatists is entirely unfounded; when the sceptic said that honey is just as much bitter as sweet and as little bitter as sweet, no thing placed behind the honey was meant there. - That for the sceptics of Greece the doctrines of all doctrines that make claims to validity for every human understanding were also an object of doubt is said to testify to their unfamiliarity with the true grounds of their doubts, and besides, at that time the particular sources of the cognitions of each science and the degrees of conviction possible in it had not yet been investigated as they are nowadays; many doctrines that now defy all rational sceptical zeal, such as physics and astronomy, were then still only an aggregate of unprovable opinions and groundless hypotheses. - This trait completes the character of this new scepticism and its difference from the old one; besides the facts of consciousness, then, physics and astronomy of more recent times would also be the sciences that defied all rational scepticism, doctrines which - once the purely mathematical element in them, which does not belong to their peculiarity, is removed - consist in a narration of sensory perceptions and an amalgamation of these with the concepts of the understanding of forces, matters, etc., in a knowledge that asserts objectivity throughout and is yet purely formal, one part of which, the narration of perceptions, has nothing at all to do with a scientific knowledge and therefore admittedly also falls outside scepticism, insofar as in the uttering of the perception nothing but its subjectivity is supposed to be expressed, - while its other part is the highest summit of a dogmatizing understanding.
What would the ancient sceptics have said to such a bastard of scepticism, which can even still get along with the glaring dogmatism of these sciences?
zh: 在我们照亮了这种怀疑论的肯定方面之后，我们转向它的否定方面，第一卷的整个第三部分就是专门讨论这个方面的。
舒尔策先生自己也感觉到，一种把不可否认的确定性归给意识的事实的怀疑论，与古代怀疑论者给我们的怀疑论概念很少一致；我们首先得听一听舒尔策先生本人对这种差别的看法。
他在导论和第三部分的第一节里对此作了说明。

他首先提醒说，事情常常是这样的：最先在真理之路上发现一个思想的人，对它的内容、根据和后果的理解远远少于在他之后细心探究其起源和意义的人；迄今为止，怀疑论的真实意图多半被认错了，等等。舒尔策先生视为真的、并且比古人的怀疑论更完善的这种怀疑论，所涉及的乃是哲学特有的判断，也就是说——用舒尔策先生表达这门科学的最终意图的话来说——这些判断规定着那种按我们意识的证词有条件地存在的东西之绝对的、至少是超感性的、即存在于意识领域之外的根据。
但仅仅属于哲学的那些判断，据说不是这种怀疑论的对象；因为它们要么表达所谓意识的事实，要么建立在分析性的思维之上；所以它们的真理即便按照怀疑论也可以被探究和看出；反之，它针对理论哲学断言：对于存在于我们意识范围之外的、或者像作者也说的那样在意识中按其存在并没有被给予的、事物存在的根据，或者对于在存在着的诸事物之外存在着的诸事物，根本什么都无法知道。
舒尔策先生自己让人对这个怀疑论概念提出反对意见：按照这个概念，经验所教导的东西中没有一样、尤其是外部感觉的总和，而且一切科学中只有哲学（因为别的科学都不与意识范围之外的事物的认识打交道）能够成为怀疑论式怀疑的对象，而古代怀疑论却扩展到两者，最古老的怀疑论至少扩展到前者。

关于这一点，舒尔策先生主要举出：怀疑论的开端和进程总是按照独断论者的僭妄来规定自己的；古代怀疑论者承认，有一种通过感官的认识，以及通过感官而对自在地存在的事物的定在和某些属性的确信，每个有理性的人在行动的生活中都得依照这种确信行事。——一种这样的确信仅仅针对行动的生活，这一点直接意味着：它与哲学毫无关系，它以及那充满事实的、有限的意识根本不是作为不可否认的确定性的原则而与理性和哲学相对立、更不是翘着脚站在它们对面的，而只是尽可能压缩地安排出来的一份贡赋，用来向客观规定的必然性纳贡；怀疑论者说，如果涉及的是在我们力量之内的事情，我们就不会选择这个或避免那个，但那些不在我们力量之内、而是按照必然性存在的事情，我们无法避免，比如饥饿、口渴、受冻；因为这些事情不能靠理性清除掉。
但同这些必然需要相关联的意识——古代怀疑论者远没有把它提升为一种作出客观主张的知识的等级；塞克斯都119)说，我们注意着显现的东西，因为我们不能完全无所行动，就按照普通的生活知性活着，并不因此作出任何意见或主张。
但在这个怀疑论里根本谈不上对事物及其属性的确信；塞克斯都说，怀疑论的标准是显现的东西（ϕαινόμενον），我们实际上把它理解为它自己的显现（ϕαντασίαν αὐτου ͂），也就是主观的东西；因为它处在确信（πείσει，但不是对一个事物的确信）和一种不由自主的被触动之中，所以不发生任何探究；它是 ἀζήτητος（德语里“怀疑”这个说法用在怀疑论上，总是偏的、不合适的）。

但怀疑论者把一切知觉都宣布为纯然的假象，而不是把不可否认的确定性归给它，并且断言：人们必须同样说出与人们就对象按其假象所说出的东西相反的东西，同样说蜂蜜是苦的正如说它是甜的，——而这一点，正如舒尔策先生自己举出的，怀疑论者最初十个真正的论式涉及的正是感性知觉的这种不可靠，对此舒尔策先生给出的理由是：感觉早在思辨哲学的最早时期就被独断论者说成一种现象，说它底下放着某种完全不同的东西，而且人们还把一种与那应当位于现象背后作为真正事物的东西的一致归给现象本身，甚至通过感觉的认识屡屡被他们说成是关于隐藏在感觉背后的对象的科学。

由于这个理由，怀疑论者攻击了独断论者关于感性认识确定性的这些学说，并否认：凭借感觉中的对象，人们能够可靠地认识那应当作为真实的、真正的、自在地存在的事物而位于这个对象背后的东西。——在这里，就古代哲学家而言，表露出来的正是舒尔策先生关于理性认识所具有的那种最粗陋的表象；但那种把怀疑论说成不是攻击感性知觉本身、而只是攻击独断论者放在它们背后和底下的东西的解释，是完全没有根据的；当怀疑论者说蜂蜜既苦又甜、既不苦也不甜时，那里并没有意指某个放在蜂蜜背后的东西。——希腊的怀疑论者把一切要求对每个人类知性有效的学说的原理也当作怀疑的对象，据说这表明他们不熟悉自己怀疑的真正根据，此外，当时还不像今天这样去研究每门科学的认识的特殊来源以及其中可能的确信程度；许多今天挡得住一切合乎理性的怀疑癖的学说，比如物理学和天文学，当时还只是不可证明的意见和无根据的假设的总和。——这个特征使这种新怀疑论的性格及其与旧怀疑论的区别得以完成；于是，除了意识的事实之外，近代的物理学和天文学也成了挡得住一切合乎理性的怀疑论的科学，成了这样一些学说——把其中纯粹数学的东西（它并不属于它们的特性）去掉之后——它们存在于对感性知觉的叙述以及这种叙述与关于力、物质等等的知性概念的一种混合之中，存在于一种处处主张客观性、却又纯粹形式的知识之中；这种知识的一个部分，即对知觉的叙述，与科学的知识根本无关，因此当然也落在怀疑论之外，因为说出知觉时应当表达的只是它的主观性，——而它的另一个部分则是独断化的知性的最高峰。
对这样一个还能同这些科学的刺眼独断论相安无事的怀疑论杂种，古代怀疑论者会说些什么呢？

en: Herr Schulze finally comes with the insecurity and incompleteness of the reports about ancient scepticism. - To be sure, we lack more determinate reports about Pyrrho, Aenesidemus and other famous older sceptics; but partly from the whole essence of this scepticism it follows that the polemical side against philosophical systems, which the scepticism of Aenesidemus, Metrodorus and later ones had, was lacking in the scepticism of Pyrrho, to which the first ten tropes belong, and partly that in the tropes of Sextus Empiricus the general essence of this scepticism is preserved for us very faithfully, so that any other elaboration of scepticism could be nothing but the repetition, occurring in application, of one and the same general manner.
zh: 舒尔策先生最后提出了关于古代怀疑论的报道之不可靠和不完整。——当然，我们缺少关于皮罗、埃奈西德穆和其他著名的较早怀疑论者的更确定的报道；但一方面，从这种怀疑论的整个本质可以看出，埃奈西德穆、梅特罗多洛斯以及更晚的人的怀疑论所具有的那种针对哲学体系的论战方面，是皮罗的怀疑论所没有的，而最初十个论式就属于皮罗；另一方面，在塞克斯都·恩披里柯的论式里，这种怀疑论的一般本质被十分忠实地保存了下来，以至于怀疑论的任何别的阐述都只能是一个同一个一般方式的重复，只是出现在应用之中。

en: In general, however, the concepts of scepticism that let it be seen only in this particular form, in which it appears as pure, mere scepticism, vanish before the standpoint of a philosophy from which it can be found as genuine scepticism even in those philosophical systems themselves which Herr Schulze and others with him can regard only as dogmatic.

Without the determination of the true relation of scepticism to philosophy and without the insight that with every true philosophy scepticism itself is most intimately one and that there is therefore a philosophy that is neither scepticism nor dogmatism and hence both at once, all the histories and tales and new editions of scepticism can lead to nothing.

The essential thing for the cognition of scepticism, this relation of scepticism to philosophy, not to a dogmatism, the recognition of a philosophy that is not a dogmatism, in general therefore the concept of a philosophy itself - that is what has escaped Herr Schulze; and if Herr Schulze could not extract the idea of philosophy from the philosophies that he takes up sceptically, then the historical element of ancient scepticism alone should at least have led him to the thought of the possibility that philosophy is something other than dogmatism, which is all he knows.

After all, even Diogenes Laertius [IX, 71 ff.] cites in his way that some name Homer as the originator of scepticism, because he speaks of the same things differently in different relations; thus many sayings of the seven sages are also sceptical, such as "Nothing in excess" and "Obligation, and ruin at its side" (i.e. every connection with something limited has its downfall in itself).

But Diogenes cites still more - Archilochus, Euripides, Zeno, Xenophanes, Democritus, Plato, etc. - as sceptics; in short, those whom Diogenes echoes had the insight that a true philosophy necessarily itself at the same time has a negative side, which is turned against everything limited and thereby against the heap of the facts of consciousness and their undeniable certainty, as well as against the narrow concepts that [occur] in those splendid doctrines which Herr Schulze holds to be inaccessible to rational scepticism - against this whole soil of finitude, on which this more recent scepticism has its essence and its truth, and is infinitely more sceptical than this scepticism.

What more perfect and self-standing document and system of genuine scepticism could we find than, in the Platonic philosophy, the Parmenides, which comprehends and destroys the whole domain of that knowledge through concepts of the understanding?

This Platonic scepticism aims not at a doubting of these truths of the understanding, which cognizes things as manifold, as wholes that consist of parts, [as] a coming-to-be and passing-away, a multiplicity, similarity, etc., and makes suchlike objective assertions, but at a complete negating of all truth of such a cognition.
This scepticism does not make out of a system a particular thing, but is itself the negative side of the cognition of the absolute and immediately presupposes reason as the positive side.

Although therefore the Platonic Parmenides appears only on the negative side, e.g. Ficinus120) recognizes for that very reason very well that whoever approaches its holy study must beforehand prepare himself through purity of mind and freedom of spirit before he dares to touch the secrets of the holy work.

Tiedemann121), however, on account of this utterance of Ficinus sees in him nothing but a man who sticks in the mire of the Neoplatonists, and in the Platonic work nothing but a heap and a cloud of rather obscure sophisms - rather ingenious for the times of a Parmenides and a Plato, but disgusting to a new metaphysician - a fault that comes from the fact that among exact philosophers the metaphysical expressions had not yet been properly determined; whoever is somewhat more practised in metaphysical matters finds that concepts that differ from one another by the whole heaven are confused, - namely, those otherwise ingenious people, Plato and Parmenides, had not yet pushed through to the philosophy that finds truth in the facts of consciousness and everywhere, only not in reason, nor to the clarity of concepts such as the understanding and a merely finite thinking establishes in the more recent sciences of physics, etc., and thinks to fetch from experience.
zh: 但总的来说，那些只让怀疑论在其表现为纯粹、单纯的怀疑论这一特殊形式中被看到的怀疑论概念，在一种哲学的立场面前消失了；从这种立场出发，怀疑论作为真正的怀疑论，甚至在舒尔策先生及其同道只能看作独断论的那些哲学体系本身之中也能找到。
如果没有对怀疑论与哲学的真正关系的规定，如果没有这种洞见——即怀疑论本身与每一种真正的哲学最内在地是一个东西，因而有一种既不是怀疑论也不是独断论、从而是两者同时的哲学——，那么关于怀疑论的一切历史和叙述以及新出的版本都无济于事。
认识怀疑论的关键，即怀疑论与哲学、而不是与某种独断论的关系，对一种不是独断论的哲学的承认，总之，哲学本身的概念，正是舒尔策先生所错过的东西；而如果舒尔策先生不能从他以怀疑方式处理的那些哲学里弄出哲学的观念，那么古代怀疑论的历史材料至少也本该把他引向这样一个想法：哲学可能是某种不同于独断论的东西，而独断论是他唯一知道的东西。
毕竟连第欧根尼·拉尔修[IX, 71 ff.]也按他自己的方式举出，有些人把荷马称为怀疑论的创始者，因为荷马对同样的事物在不同的关系下说法不同；同样，七贤的许多格言也是怀疑论的，比如“勿过度”和“作保，灾祸就在旁边”（即任何与有限者的结合都自含其覆灭）。

但第欧根尼还把阿尔基洛科斯、欧里庇得斯、芝诺、克塞诺芬尼、德谟克利特、柏拉图等等举为怀疑论者；总之，第欧根尼所附和的那些人有这样的洞见：一种真正的哲学必然自身同时有一个否定方面，这个方面针对一切有限的东西，从而针对意识的事实这一大堆东西及其不可否认的确定性，也针对那些在舒尔策先生认为合乎理性的怀疑论无法企及的光辉学说中出现的狭隘概念，针对这个有限性的整个地基——这种较新的怀疑论就在这个地基上有其本质和真理——，并且比这种怀疑论无限地更怀疑。
在柏拉图哲学中，我们还能找到什么比《巴门尼德》更完善、更独立自存的真正怀疑论的文献和体系呢——它用知性概念把那种知识的整个领域都包住并加以摧毁？
这种柏拉图式的怀疑论并不针对对这些知性真理的怀疑——知性把事物认识为杂多的、认识为由部分构成的整体、认识为生成和消逝、多、相似等等，并作出诸如此类的客观主张——，而是针对对这种认识的一切真理的彻底否定。
这种怀疑论并不从体系里弄出一个特殊的东西，而是它本身就是对绝对者的认识的否定方面，并且直接以理性为肯定方面而把它预设下来。
因此，尽管柏拉图式的《巴门尼德》只出现在否定方面，例如斐奇诺120)就正因如此而很清楚地认识到，凡是着手对它作神圣研究的人，都必须先以心地的纯洁和精神的自由来预备自己，然后才敢去碰这件神圣作品的秘密。

而蒂德曼121)由于斐奇诺的这番话，在他身上看到的只是一个泡在新柏拉图主义者的污泥里的人，在柏拉图的作品里看到的只是一堆和一团相当晦涩的诡辩——对一个巴门尼德和柏拉图的时代来说相当尖刻，却使一个新形而上学家感到厌恶——；这个错误来自：严谨的哲学家还没有把形而上学的表述恰当规定下来；在形而上学的事情上稍微练达的人就会发现，那些彼此相差整个天地的概念被混淆了，——就是说，那些本来很尖刻的人，柏拉图和巴门尼德，还没有推进到那样一种哲学，它到处、在意识的事实里寻找真理，唯独不在理性里寻找，也还没有达到知性和一种纯粹有限的思想在较新的物理学等科学里所确定下来、并以为可以从经验中取来的那种概念清晰性。

en: This scepticism, which appears in its pure, explicit shape in the Parmenides, is, however, to be found implicitly in every genuine philosophical system, for it is the free side of every philosophy; if in any proposition that expresses a rational cognition the reflected element in it, the concepts contained in it, are isolated and the way they are connected is considered, then it must show itself that these concepts are at the same time sublated or are united in such a way that they contradict themselves, otherwise it would not be a rational but an understanding proposition.

Spinoza begins his Ethics with the explanation: "By cause of itself I understand [that] whose essence involves existence, or that whose nature can be conceived only as existing." - But now the concept of essence or of nature can only be posited by abstracting from existence; the one excludes the other; the one is determinable only insofar as there is an opposition to the other; if both are posited as connected as one, their connection contains a contradiction, and both are at the same time negated.
Or if another proposition of Spinoza reads thus: "God is the immanent, not the transient cause of the world" [Ethics I, Prop.

XVIII], then he, in that he posits the cause as immanent, thus the cause as one with the effect - because the cause is cause only insofar as it is opposed to the effect -, has negated the concept of cause and effect; just as dominant is the antinomy of the one and the many; unity is posited as identical with the many, the substance with its attributes.

Since every such rational proposition can be resolved into two that absolutely conflict with each other - e.g. God is cause and God is not cause; he is one and not one, many and not many; he has an essence which, because essence is conceivable only in opposition to form and form must be posited as identical with essence, itself again falls away, etc. -, the principle of scepticism: παντὶ λόγῳ λόγος ἴσος ἀντίϰειται, comes on the scene in its full strength.

The so-called proposition of contradiction is therefore so far from being of even formal truth for reason that, on the contrary, every rational proposition must, with regard to the concepts, contain an offence against it; a proposition is merely formal means for reason: posited by itself alone, without equally asserting the proposition contradictorily opposed to it, it is for that very reason false.

To acknowledge the proposition of contradiction as formal thus means to recognize it at the same time as false. - Since every genuine philosophy has this negative side or eternally sublates the proposition of contradiction, whoever has the inclination can immediately lift out this negative side and construct a scepticism out of each one.
zh: 这种在其纯粹而明确的形态中出现在《巴门尼德》里的怀疑论，其实在每一个真正的哲学体系里都隐含地可以找到，因为它是每一种哲学的自由方面；如果在某个表达理性认识的命题里，把其中被反思到的东西、即它包含的那些概念孤立起来看，并考察它们被联结的方式，那就必定会表明：这些概念同时被扬弃了，或者以这样一种方式被联合起来，以致它们互相矛盾，否则它就不是一个理性的命题，而是一个知性的命题。
斯宾诺莎的《伦理学》以这样的说明开始：“所谓自因，我理解为[那种]其本质包含存在的东西，或者那种其本性只能被设想为存在的东西。”——但现在，本质或本性的概念只有通过从存在中抽象出来才能被设定；一个排斥另一个；一个只有在对另一个有对立时才是可规定的；如果两者作为一而被联结起来设定，那么它们的联结就包含一个矛盾，两者同时被否定了。
或者，如果斯宾诺莎的另一个命题这样说：“上帝是世界的内在原因，而不是过渡性的原因”[《伦理学》I，命题
XVIII]，那么他由于把原因设定为内在的，也就是把原因设定为与效果同一的——因为原因只有在与效果相对立时才成其为原因——，就否定了原因和效果的概念；同样占统治地位的是一与多的二律背反；统一性被设定为与多同一，实体被设定为与其属性同一。
既然每一个这样的理性命题都可以分解为两个绝对互相冲突的命题——例如：上帝是原因，上帝不是原因；他是一又不是一，是多又不是多；他有一个本质，而这个本质由于本质只有在与形式的对立中才可以被概念把握、而形式又必须被设定为与本质同一，就自身重新消失了，等等——，那么怀疑论的原则：παντὶ λόγῳ λόγος ἴσος ἀντίϰειται，就以它的全部力量出场了。
所以，所谓的矛盾命题远不是对理性也具有哪怕形式上的真理，相反，每一个理性命题就概念而言都必定包含对它的违犯；一个命题仅仅是形式的，对理性来说意味着：它单独自在地被设定，而没有同样主张那个与它矛盾地相对立的命题，就正因如此而是假的。
所以，把矛盾命题承认为形式的，同时就意味着把它认作假的。——既然每一种真正的哲学都有这个否定方面，或者说永恒地扬弃矛盾命题，那么谁有兴趣，谁就可以直接把这个否定方面提取出来，并从每一种哲学里弄出一套怀疑论。

en: It is quite incomprehensible how in Herr Schulze, even through Sextus, the concept has not come about even in general, that besides scepticism and dogmatism there is yet a third thing, namely a philosophy; right in the first lines Sextus divides the philosophers into dogmatists, academics and sceptics, and where throughout his whole work he has to do with the dogmatists, he by no means thinks that he has thereby also refuted the Academy.

This relation of scepticism to the Academy has itself been discussed enough; it has occasioned a dispute famous in the history of scepticism, and this relation of pure scepticism and its embarrassment is its most interesting side.
Yet in order not to do Herr Schulze an injustice, it must be mentioned that he was indeed made attentive by Sextus to a relation of the Academy to scepticism.
But how does Herr Schulze take up this relation, and what Sextus says about it?

In the note (Part I, S. 608), in which Herr Schulze dispatches the matter, he says that through the doctrine of Arcesilaus (the founder of the middle Academy) doubting the truth of the doctrines of dogmatism has now indeed been made into a business stripped of every application of reason, because it sublates itself again and reason here hears nothing at all any more.

Then Herr Schulze relates that Sextus (Pyrrhonian Hypotyposes I, 33) wants the doctrine of Arcesilaus to be distinguished from scepticism on the ground that, according to the doctrine of Arcesilaus and of Carneades, even this itself, that everything is uncertain, must again be declared uncertain; such a business of doubting, Herr Schulze adds from his own resources, is stripped of all reason.
zh: 完全不可理解的是，舒尔策先生那里竟然连通过塞克斯都都没有形成哪怕一般性的这样一个概念：在怀疑论和独断论之外还有第三种东西，也就是一种哲学；塞克斯都在开篇头几行就把哲学家分为独断论者、学园派和怀疑论者，而他在整部著作中打交道的是独断论者，他根本不认为自己顺带也驳倒了学园派。
怀疑论与学园派的这种关系本身已经谈得够多了；它引起了一场在怀疑论史上著名的争论，而纯粹怀疑论的这种关系以及它的窘境，正是它最有意思的一面。
不过，为了不冤枉舒尔策先生，也得提一句：他确实是通过塞克斯都才注意到学园派与怀疑论之间有某种关系的。
可是，舒尔策先生是怎样理解这种关系以及塞克斯都对此所说的话的呢？
在（第一部分，S. 608）那条把这件事打发掉的注释里，他说：由于阿尔克西拉乌斯（中期学园派的创立者）的学说，对独断论学说之真理的怀疑如今固然变成了一桩被剥夺了一切理性运用的行当，因为它又把自己扬弃掉，而理性在这里根本听不到任何东西了。
接着舒尔策先生叙述说，塞克斯都（《皮浪学说纲要》I, 33）要人把阿尔克西拉乌斯的学说与怀疑论区别开来，理由是：按照阿尔克西拉乌斯和卡尔涅阿德斯的学说，就连“一切都不确定”这一点本身也必须重新被宣布为不确定；舒尔策先生自己添上一句说，这样一种怀疑的行当被剥夺了一切理性。

en: As regards first of all the historical side, one does not trust one's eyes when one reads such a ground for the exclusion of the doctrine of Arcesilaus from scepticism ascribed to Sextus.

For it is the sceptics themselves who express themselves most definitely, as Herr Schulze himself cites at the beginning of the note, to the effect that their customary ϕωναί - everything is false, nothing is true, one no more than the other, etc. - also include themselves again, συμπεϱιγϱάϕειν (Pyrrh.
Hyp.

I. 7), and again to sublate themselves, ὑϕ' ἑαυτω ͂ν αὐτὰς ἀναιϱείσϑαι ἐμπεϱιγϱαϕομένας ἐϰείνοις πεϱὶ ὡν λέγεται [I, 206] -, a doctrine which, besides lying in scepticism itself, was also outwardly absolutely necessary against the dogmatists, who reproached the sceptics with nevertheless having a dogma, “nothing to determine” or “none is truer”, and likewise for the distinction from other philosophers, e.g. (c. 30) the Democritean ones, to whom the sceptical expression “one no more than the other” - e.g. honey is no more sweet than bitter - belonged.

The sceptics distinguished themselves by this, that they said a dogma lies herein: it is neither of the two; they, by contrast, show through that expression “one as little as the other” that they do not know whether the appearance is both or neither of the two.

Thus Sextus (c. 33) also distinguishes the sceptics from the new Academy of Carneades, whose fundamental proposition consists in this, that everything is incomprehensible; perhaps, he says, it is different only in this, that it expresses that incomprehensibility assertorically.

As for what Herr Schulze says in restriction of those sceptical expressions - that Sextus presumably only wanted to teach that the sceptic determines nothing about the transcendental constitution of things, neither in a positive nor in a negative way -, no opposition at all is to be seen in it to that assertion of the sceptics and of Arcesilaus, that a sceptical expression includes and sublates itself within itself.
And what then is the transcendental constitution of things supposed to mean? does the transcendental not lie precisely in this, that there are neither things nor a constitution of things?

Sextus was therefore in and for himself quite remote from distinguishing the doctrine of Arcesilaus from scepticism on the ground Herr Schulze states, for it was verbally that of scepticism; Sextus says himself that it seems to him to agree so much with the Pyrrhonian λόγοις that it is almost one and the same ἀγωγή122) as the sceptical one, unless one wants to say that Arcesilaus declares the ἐποχήν to be good and in accordance with nature, but assent to be evil, which is an assertion, whereas the sceptics on the contrary assert nothing even about this.

The distinction of which Sextus thinks that it can still be made thus has precisely the opposite ground; according to Herr Schulze this Academy would have been declared by Sextus to be too sceptical; but Sextus, as we have seen, finds it too little sceptical.

Besides the distinction adduced, Sextus brings in a still worse ground, which is out for applause, namely that Arcesilaus, if one may believe what is said of him, was a Pyrrhonian only for the start, but in truth a dogmatist; for he used the aporematic only in order to test his pupils, whether they have capacity for the Platonic doctrines, and for that reason he was held to be an aporetic; but to those found capable he taught the Platonic. - On account of the difficult side of scepticism, which for him lay in the relation to the Academy, Sextus treats Plato and the Academies very extensively.

It lies only in the complete lack of the concept of the true ground of this difficulty and of philosophy, if Herr Schulze can believe himself freed from the regard for the Academy by the chatter which he cites on this point in this very note from Stäudlin's History of Scepticism123).

But, says Herr Schulze, it has recently already been remarked by several, especially by Stäudlin, that the spirit which animated the middle and newer Academy is wholly different from the spirit which guided the sceptics in their investigations; the adherents of the former were really nothing more than sophistical babblers, who aimed solely at fallacies and delusions and used philosophy, as well as the whole dispute of the sceptics with the dogmatists as it was conducted at the time, only as a means of their main purpose, namely the art of persuading others, of shining and of causing a sensation, and had no sense at all for the investigation of truth for its own sake. - Even if such an accusation were not already in and for itself as hollow and disgusting as it is, there would still remain the older Academy and Plato himself; there remains philosophy in general, which is no dogmatism, which would have had to be taken into account; but more regard for philosophy than we have cited from this note we have not been able to find.
zh: 先说历史方面，当人们读到这样一条把阿尔克西拉乌斯的学说从怀疑论中排除出去的理由被算到塞克斯都头上时，简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。
因为正是怀疑论者自己——就像舒尔策先生在注释开头自己引证的那样——最明确地表示：他们那些常用的 ϕωναί——一切皆假，无物为真，这一个并不比那一个更是如此，等等——也把自己重新包含进去，συμπεϱιγϱάϕειν（Pyrrh.
Hyp.

I. 7），并且又把自己扬弃掉，ὑϕ' ἑαυτω ͂ν αὐτὰς ἀναιϱείσϑαι ἐμπεϱιγϱαϕομένας ἐϰείνοις πεϱὶ ὡν λέγεται [I, 206]——，这个学说，除了就包含在怀疑论本身之中，对外针对独断论者也完全是必要的——他们指责怀疑论者毕竟还是有一个教条，即“什么都不去规定”或“没有一个更真”——，同时它对于同其他哲学家区别开来也同样是必要的，例如（c. 30）德谟克利特派，“这一个并不比那一个更是如此”这个怀疑论说法——例如蜂蜜并不比苦的更甜——本来就是属于他们的。
怀疑论者以此把自己区别开来：他们说这里头有一个教条，即它两者都不是；而他们则通过“这一个并不比那一个更是如此”这个说法表明，他们并不知道现象是两者兼是，还是两者都不是。
塞克斯都（c. 33）也这样把怀疑论者与卡尔涅阿德斯的新学园派区别开来，后者的根本命题就在于：一切都是不可把握的；他说，它也许只是在这点上不同，即它是把那种不可把握当作主张说出来的。
舒尔策先生为了限制那些怀疑论说法而说的话——即塞克斯都大概只是想教导说：怀疑论者对于事物的先验的性状，既不以肯定的方式，也不以否定的方式作任何规定——，这里面根本看不出与怀疑论者和阿尔克西拉乌斯那个主张有什么对立，那个主张是说：一种怀疑论说法在自身中把自己包含并扬弃。
那么，事物的先验的性状又该是什么意思呢？先验的东西难道不恰恰就在于：既没有事物，也没有事物的性状吗？
所以，塞克斯都本来就根本不会按舒尔策先生所说的那条理由，把阿尔克西拉乌斯的学说与怀疑论区别开来，因为它字面上就是怀疑论的学说；塞克斯都自己说，它在他看来与皮浪派的 λόγοις 一致得几乎与怀疑论是同一种、同一个 ἀγωγή122)，除非人们要说：阿尔克西拉乌斯宣称 ἐποχήν 是好的、合乎本性的，而赞同是坏的——这就是一个主张，而怀疑论者对这种东西也同样不作任何主张性的断言。
塞克斯都认为还可以作出的那种区分，其理由恰恰相反；按舒尔策先生的说法，这个学园派会被塞克斯都宣布为过于怀疑论；但塞克斯都——如我们所见——倒觉得它太不怀疑论。

除了上面举出的那个区分，塞克斯都还搬出一条更糟的理由，它冲着的是掌声：阿尔克西拉乌斯——如果人们可以相信关于他所说的那些话——只是起步、起跑时算个皮浪派，真正说来却是个独断论者；因为他用那种疑难的做法只是为了考验学生，看他们有没有能力接受柏拉图的学说，他也因此被当成一个疑难派；而对那些考出来有能力的人，他教的却是柏拉图的东西。——由于怀疑论棘手的那一面在他看来就在于与学园派的关系，塞克斯都极为详尽地讨论了柏拉图和各个学园派。
舒尔策先生竟能以为，凭他紧接着在同一条注释里从施托伊德林的《怀疑论史》123) 引来的那番废话，就摆脱了对学园派的顾及，这只说明他完全缺乏关于这种棘手的困难的真实根据的概念，也完全缺乏哲学。

可是，舒尔策先生说，近来已经有好些人、尤其是施托伊德林指出：使中期和新学园派活跃起来的那个精神，与在研究中引导怀疑论者的那个精神完全不同；前者的追随者现实地不过是些诡辩的空谈家，一味追求谬误推论和障眼把戏，把哲学以及怀疑论者与独断论者之间当时所进行的那整场争论，只当作达成他们主要目的的手段，也就是当作说服别人、炫耀自己和引起轰动的本领来使用，对于为真理本身而研究真理则毫无感觉。——即便这样一种指控本身并不像它实际上那样空洞和恶心，那也还剩下了更早的学园派和柏拉图本人；还剩下了哲学本身，而哲学并不是什么独断论，本来是应当顾及它的；但我们没能找到比我们从这条注释里引出的更多的对哲学的顾及。

en: In antiquity, by contrast, consciousness of this relation of scepticism to Platonism was very developed; a great dispute had prevailed about it, in that one party declared Plato to be a dogmatist, another party declared him to be a sceptic (Diogenes Laertius [III] 51, Plato).

Since the records of the dispute are lost to us, we cannot judge how far the inner true relation of scepticism to philosophy came to be discussed in it, and how far the dogmatists, who claimed Plato for dogmatism, as the sceptics likewise did, understood this in the sense that scepticism itself belongs to philosophy or not.

Sextus appeals to a further elaboration of the matter in his sceptical commentaries, which have not come down to us; in the Hypotyposes I, 222, he says he wants to present the main point following Aenesidemus and Menodotus, who in this dispute were the leaders on the side of the sceptics; Plato is a dogmatist, because when he [says] that ideas, a providence, a preference of a virtuous life over a vicious one are, he either dogmatises, if he recognises them as existing; or if he assents to the more convincing (πιϑανοτέϱοις), then, by preferring something to another for the sake of conviction or non-conviction, he falls out of the sceptical character.
zh: 相反，在古代，关于怀疑论与柏拉图主义之间的这种关系，意识是很发达的；围绕它曾有过一场大争论，一部分人把柏拉图说成独断论者，另一部分人则把他说成怀疑论者（第欧根尼·拉尔修 [III] 51，柏拉图）。
由于这场争论的文献对我们已经失传，我们无法判断：怀疑论与哲学的内在真实关系在其中被谈到什么程度，以及那些把柏拉图划归独断论的独断论者——怀疑论者也同样这么做——是在什么意义上理解这件事的，即怀疑论本身究竟属不属于哲学。

塞克斯都援引他那些怀疑论注释中对这件事的进一步阐述，而那些注释没有流传到我们手里；在《纲要》I, 222 中他说，他要按埃涅西德摩斯和梅诺多托斯——他们在这场争论中是怀疑论者一方的头面人物——来陈述要点；柏拉图是个独断论者，因为当他说有观念、有天意、有德性生活在恶的生活面前的优势时，他要么是在独断地立论，即把它们承认为存在着的；要么，如果他赞同那更可信的东西（πιϑανοτέϱοις），那么他由于为了信服或不信服而把某物置于另一物之前，就落到了怀疑论品格之外。

en: This distinction of Platonism from scepticism is either a merely formal carping which, in the alleged preference, censures nothing but the form of consciousness - for the sceptic's obedience to necessity and to the laws of his country was just such a preference, only an unconscious one -, or, if it is directed against the reality of the idea itself, it concerns reason's cognition of itself; and on this the peculiarity of pure scepticism, which separates itself from philosophy, must show itself.

Sextus comes to this cognition of reason in the first book against the logicians (I, 310), after he had previously disputed the criterion of truth in general from the philosophers' discord about it, and then in particular the truth of sensory cognition.

What he says against it, namely that reason does not cognise itself through itself (ὅτι οὐδ' ἑαυτη ͂ς ἐπιγνώμων ἐστὶν ἡ διάνοια... , ὁ νου ͂ς ἑαυτὸν ϰαταλαμβάνεται), is bare enough, so that if the more recent sceptics want to combat reason's self-cognition, they will have to bring forward something better, unless they make it easier for themselves by sparing themselves this trouble entirely, in that they wholly ignore reason and its self-cognising and, stuck behind the Gorgon shield, immediately - not through any malicious distortion or art, not as if they saw it differently beforehand, but in the gaze itself - transform the rational, subjectively expressed in the understanding, objectively into stones, and call that of which they suspect that it goes beyond understanding and stone enthusiasm and imagination. - Sextus, at least, still knows of reason and its self-cognition.

What he brings forward about its possibility is the following shallow reasoning, to which he now himself brings precisely the reflection-concepts of whole and parts, which - as Plato in the Parmenides - he destroys in his books against the physicists.
If reason comprehends itself, then either, insofar as it comprehends itself, it must be the whole that comprehends itself, or it is not the whole and uses only a part for this.

If now it is the whole that comprehends itself, then the comprehending and the comprehending one is the whole; but if the whole is the comprehending one, then nothing more remains over for the comprehended; but it is quite irrational that the comprehending should be, but not that which is comprehended.
But reason also cannot use a part of itself for this; for how is the part to comprehend itself?

If it is a whole, then nothing remains over for what is to be comprehended; if again with a part, how is this again to comprehend itself? and so on into infinity, so that the comprehending is without principle, since either no first is found which is to undertake the comprehending, or there is nothing that is to be comprehended. - One sees that reason is converted into an absolutely subjective, which, if it is posited as whole, leaves nothing more over for what is to be comprehended.

Then (and now come still better grounds, which drag reason down, as before into the concept of whole and parts and of an either absolute subjectivity or absolute objectivity, now into the appearance of a determinate place): if reason comprehends itself, it will thereby also comprehend together the place in which it is, for every comprehending one comprehends together with a determinate place; but if reason comprehends the place in which it is together with itself, then the philosophers ought not to be at variance about it, in that some say that place is the head, others the breast, and in particular some the brain, others the cerebral membrane, others the heart, others the passages of the liver or else some other part of the body; about this the dogmatic philosophers are at variance.
Reason, then, does not comprehend itself.
zh: 这种把柏拉图主义与怀疑论区别开来的做法，要么只是一种纯形式的挑刺，它在所说的优先选择上挑剔的不过是意识的形式——因为怀疑论者对必然性和祖国法律的服从，也是同样一种优先选择，只不过是无意识的——；要么，如果它是针对观念本身的实在性的，那它涉及的就是理性对自身的认识；而纯粹怀疑论——那种与哲学分离开来的纯粹怀疑论——的特殊性，正必须在这里显现出来。
塞克斯都是在《反逻辑学家》第一书（I, 310）里谈到理性这种自我认识的，此前他已经根据哲学家们关于真理标准的争执否定了这个标准本身，接着又特别否定了感性认识的真理。

他针对这一点所说的，即理性并不通过自身认识自身（ὅτι οὐδ' ἑαυτη ͂ς ἐπιγνώμων ἐστὶν ἡ διάνοια... , ὁ νου ͂ς ἑαυτὸν ϰαταλαμβάνεται），够干瘪的：如果新近的怀疑论者要反对理性的自我认识，他们总得拿出点更好的东西来；除非他们图省事，干脆把这桩麻烦整个省掉——完全不去理会理性及其自我认识，躲在戈耳工盾牌后面，直接地，不是通过什么恶意的歪曲和手法，不是仿佛他们先前看到的不是这样，而就在看的那一眼里，就把合乎理性的东西，主观上表达为知性，客观上变成石头，并且把他们隐约觉得超出知性和石头的东西，叫作狂热和想象力。——塞克斯都毕竟还知道有理性及其自我认识。
他关于这种自我认识的可能性所提出的，是下面这套浅薄的推理；而他所搬出来的，恰恰是整体与部分这些反思概念——就像柏拉图在《巴门尼德》里那样，他在《反物理学家》诸书中把这些概念摧毁掉了。
如果理性以概念把握自己，那么它要么——就它以概念把握自己而言——必须是那个以概念把握自己的整体，要么就不是整体，只用自己的一部分来做这件事。
如果现在以概念把握自己的是整体，那么概念把握和以概念把握者就是整体；但如果整体就是以概念把握者，那么留给被以概念把握者的就什么都不剩了；可是，以概念把握者存在，而被以概念把握的东西却不存在，这完全是不合理性的。
但理性也不能用自己的一部分来做这件事；因为部分又怎么以概念把握自己呢？
如果它是一个整体，那么留给有待以概念把握者的就什么都不剩了；如果又是用一个部分，那这个部分又怎么以概念把握自己呢？如此下去直到无限，以致概念把握没有原则，因为要么找不到一个最先的、来从事概念把握的东西，要么就没有什么应当被以概念把握。——可以看到，理性被颠倒成一个绝对主观的东西，它一旦被设定为整体，就不给有待以概念把握者留下任何东西了。

接着（现在还有更好的理由出场，它们把理性——像先前拽进整体与部分的概念、拽进要么绝对主观性要么绝对客观性那样——如今又拽进一个特定位置的显现）：如果理性以概念把握自己本身，那它就会连自己所在的位置也一并以概念把握，因为每个以概念把握者都连同某个特定位置一起以概念把握；可是，如果理性把自身所在的位置连同自己一起以概念把握，那么哲学家们就不该为这个位置争执不下，因为有些人说那个位置是头，另一些人说是胸，具体到细处，有人说是脑，有人说是脑膜，有人说是心，有人说是肝的通道或身体别的什么部位；在这一点上，独断论的哲学家们是争执不下的。
所以，理性并不以概念把握自己本身。

en: This is what Sextus brings forward against the self-cognition of reason; it is an example of all the weapons of scepticism against reason; they consist in an application of concepts to it, whereby it becomes easy to show up reason — transferred into finitude and, as Herr Schulze does, made into things — as something opposed to an other, which must likewise be posited, but is not posited by that singleness.

The most ordinary thing of all, namely the appeal to the disunity of the philosophers among themselves, Sextus likewise sets out at length immediately after the passage cited — a chatter that the moral dogmatists share with scepticism against speculation, as Xenophon too already puts it into Socrates' mouth, and which presents itself most readily to the superficial view that sticks to the words.

Even if therefore this scepticism has torn itself away from philosophy, namely from that philosophy which at the same time includes scepticism within itself, and has isolated itself, it has nevertheless recognized this distinction from dogmatism and from philosophy (the latter under the name of the academic) as well as the great agreement of the latter with it, of which the more recent scepticism on the other hand knows nothing.
zh: 这就是塞克斯都用来反对理性的自我认识的东西；它是怀疑论反对理性的一切武器的一个例子；这些武器在于把概念应用到理性上，于是要指出下面这点就变得容易了：被移置到有限性之中、并且像舒尔策先生所做的那样被弄成诸多事物的理性，是一个与另一个东西相对立的东西，而那另一个东西同样必须被设定，却没有通过那种个别性被设定。
一切之中最寻常的，就是援引哲学家们彼此的不一致，塞克斯都在刚引的那段话之后也同样长篇地加以展开——这是一种空谈，道德独断论者与怀疑论一起用它来对付思辨，正如色诺芬也早已把它放进苏格拉底嘴里，而它最容易被那种黏在字面上的肤浅看法接受。
所以，即使这种怀疑论从哲学——即那种同时把怀疑论包含在自身之内的哲学——那里挣脱出来并孤立了自己，它毕竟还是认识到独断论与哲学（后者以学院派之名出现）之间的这个区别，以及后者与它的高度一致，而较新的怀疑论对此却一无所知。

en: But apart from the scepticism that is one with philosophy, the scepticism torn away from it can be twofold: either it is not directed against reason, or it is directed against it.

From the shape in which Sextus presents to us the scepticism separated from philosophy and turned against it, the old genuine scepticism can be strikingly separated out — the scepticism that indeed did not have a positive side like philosophy, but asserted a pure negativity in relation to knowledge, yet was just as little directed against philosophy; just as separately stands its hostile direction, added later, directed partly against philosophy, partly against dogmatism.

Its turning against the same, as this dogmatism too became such, shows how it has kept step with the common degeneration of philosophy and of the world in general, until finally in the most recent times it sinks down so far together with dogmatism that now for both the facts of consciousness have undeniable certainty and for both truth lies in temporality, so that, because the extremes touch, in these happy times the great goal is again attained on their side, namely that downwards dogmatism and scepticism coincide and both extend to each other the most friendly and brotherly hand.
The Schulzean scepticism unites the crudest dogmatism with itself, and the Krugian dogmatism at the same time carries that scepticism within itself.
zh: 可是，除了与哲学合为一体的那种怀疑论，从哲学那里被撕扯下来的怀疑论还可以是双重的：它要么不是针对理性的，要么是针对理性的。
从塞克斯都向我们展示的那种与哲学分离并转而反对哲学的怀疑论形态中，可以醒目地析出古老的真正怀疑论，它虽然不像哲学那样有一个肯定面，而是在与知识的关系中主张一种纯粹的否定性，但同样不是针对哲学的；同样被分离出来的，还有它后来才添上的敌意倾向，一部分针对哲学，一部分针对独断论。
它转而反对哲学，而这种独断论也变成了这样，这表明它是怎样与哲学乃至与整个世界的共同退化保持同步的，直到它最终在最新时代与独断论一起沉得如此之低，以致现在对两者来说意识的事实都具有不可否认的确定性，而对两者来说真理都落在时间性之中，于是，因为极端相互接触，在这些幸运的时代里从它们这方面又重新达到了那个伟大目标：向下看时，独断论和怀疑论合而为一，两者彼此伸出最亲如兄弟的手。
舒尔策式的怀疑论把最粗陋的独断论与自己结合在一起，而克鲁格式的独断论同时又把那种怀疑论包含在自身之内。

en: Sextus presents to us the maxims of scepticism in seventeen tropes, whose difference marks out precisely for us the distinction of his scepticism from the old one, which indeed stood by itself, without philosophical knowledge, but all the same falls entirely within philosophy, and is quite identical especially with the old philosophy, which had less to do with subjectivity.
zh: 塞克斯都把怀疑论的准则以十七个论式的形式摆在我们面前，这些论式的差异恰好向我们标明了他的怀疑论与古老怀疑论的区别，后者虽然独立自存，没有哲学知识，却完全同时落在哲学之内，并且尤其与那种较少同主体性打交道的古老哲学完全是一回事。

en: To the old scepticism belong the first ten of the seventeen tropes, to which only the much later sceptics — Sextus says simply the newer ones; Diogenes names Agrippa, who lived about five hundred years after Pyrrho — added five; the two that came in addition [ap]pear again later; Diogenes does not mention them at all, Sextus too sets them apart, and they are insignificant.
zh: 十七个论式中的前十个属于古老的怀疑论，只有晚得多的一些怀疑论者才给它们添上了五个——塞克斯都笼统地说是较新的怀疑论者；第欧根尼举出阿格里帕，此人约生活在皮罗之后五百年；后来还加上来的那两个则[出]现得更晚；第欧根尼根本未提及它们，塞克斯都也把它们单独分出，而它们无关紧要。

en: Now these ten articles, to which the old scepticism confined itself, are, like all philosophy in general, directed against the dogmatism of ordinary consciousness itself; they ground the uncertainty about the finite things in which that consciousness is unconsciously caught, and this indifference of spirit, before which everything that appearance or the understanding gives is made to waver — in which wavering of everything finite, according to the sceptics, the ἀταραξία acquired through reason enters as the shadow follows the body.

As Apelles, when he was painting a horse and could not bring off the representation of the foam, gave it up, threw at the picture the sponge with which he had wiped the colours from his brush, and thereby hit the copy of the foam, so in the mixture of everything that appears and is thought the sceptics find the true, that equanimity acquired through reason, which to possess by nature constitutes the difference of the animal from the human being, and which Pyrrho once on board ship showed to his companions, who were faint-hearted in the violent storm, with a calm mind, pointing to a pig that was eating in the ship, with the words: the wise man must stand in such ataraxia.
This scepticism therefore had its positive side entirely and solely in the character and its complete indifference toward the necessity of nature.
zh: 那么，古老怀疑论所限于其中的这十条，就像一般的一切哲学一样，是针对普通意识自身的独断论的；它们为普通意识无意识地困于其中的那些有限之物的不确定性提供根据，也为精神的这种无差别提供根据——在精神的这种无差别面前，现象或知性所给出的一切都被弄得摇摆不定；而按照怀疑论者的说法，在一切有限之物的这种摇摆之中，通过理性而获得的 ἀταραξία 便像影子跟着身体一样随之进入。
正如阿佩莱斯在画一匹马、却画不出泡沫的样子时，放弃了这个打算，把他擦掉笔上颜料的那块海绵朝画上扔去，就此打中了泡沫的摹本，同样，怀疑论者在一切显现之物和思想之物的混合中找到了真的东西，即那种通过理性而获得的平静——天生就拥有它，构成了动物与人的区别——而皮罗当年在船上，心平气和地指着船里一头正在吃东西的猪，用这样的话把这种平静指给在猛烈风暴中胆怯的同伴们看：智者必须处于这样的不动心之中。
所以，这种怀疑论的肯定面完全只在于性格，以及性格对自然必然性的完全漠然。

en: From a brief mention of the ten points that ground the scepticism's ἐποχή, its direction against the security of things and of the facts of consciousness will immediately emerge; for the insecurity of all things and the necessity of the ἐποχή is demonstrated 1. from the difference of the animals, 2. of human beings, 3. of the organization of the senses, 4. of circumstances, 5. of positions, distances and places, 6. from mixtures (through which nothing presents itself to the sense purely), 7. from the different sizes and qualities of things, 8. from relation (namely that everything is only in relation to an other), 9. from the more frequent or rarer occurrence, 10.
[from the difference] of culture, of customs, laws, mythical belief, of prejudices.
zh: 只要简短提及为怀疑论的 ἐποχή 提供根据的那十点，它针对事物的可靠性和意识的事实的指向就会直接显出来；因为一切事物的不可靠和 ἐποχή 的必然性是这样得到证明的：1. 从动物的差异，2. 从人的差异，3. 从感官组织的差异，4. 从处境的差异，5. 从位置、距离和地点的差异，6. 从混合（通过混合，没有什么东西纯粹地呈现给感官），7. 从事物各种不同的大小和性状，8. 从关系（即一切东西都只是在与另一个东西的关系之中），9. 从事件发生得更频繁或更稀少，10.
[从]教养、习俗、法律、神话信仰、偏见的[差异]。

en: Concerning their form, Sextus himself remarks that all these tropes can properly be reduced to a triplicity: one [trope] of the difference of the cognizing subject, one of the cognized object, and one composed of both.

Necessarily, too, in the execution several must flow into one another. — In the first two tropes, the difference of the animals and of human beings, Sextus already speaks of the difference of the organs, which properly belongs under the third; the most extensive, Sextus notes, is the eighth point, which concerns the conditionedness of every finite thing by an other, or that each is only in relation to an other.

One sees that they are picked up at random and presuppose an undeveloped reflection, or rather an absence of purpose in reflection with regard to a doctrine of its own, and a clumsiness that would not be present if scepticism had already had to do with the criticizing of the sciences.
zh: 关于它们的形式，塞克斯都自己指出，所有这些论式其实都可以归结为三重：一个[论式]是认识着的主体的差异，一个是被认识的客体的差异，一个由两者组合而成。
在具体展开时，也必然会有好几个论式相互交融。——在头两个论式，即动物和人的差异那里，塞克斯都已经谈到器官的差异，而器官的差异其实属于第三个论式；塞克斯都指出，最宽泛的是第八点，它涉及每个有限之物都受另一个东西制约，或者说每个东西都只是在与另一个东西的关系之中。
人们看得出，它们是被随手抓来的，并且预设了一种未展开的反思，或者更确切地说，预设了反思在一种自己的学说方面毫无目的，还预设了一种笨拙——假如怀疑论早已同诸科学的批判打过交道，这种笨拙就不会存在。

en: But the content of these tropes proves still more how far removed they are from a tendency against philosophy and how they go entirely and solely against the dogmatism of ordinary common sense; not a single one concerns reason and its cognition, but all of them concern exclusively the finite and the cognition of the finite, the understanding.

Their content is in part empirical, and to that extent does not concern speculation at all in itself; in part it concerns relation in general, or that everything actual is conditioned by an other, and to that extent it expresses a principle of reason.

This scepticism is accordingly not at all turned against philosophy, but, in a manner that is precisely not philosophical but popular, against ordinary common sense or ordinary consciousness, which holds fast to the given, the fact, the finite (let this finite be called appearance or concept) and clings to it as to something certain, secure, eternal; those sceptical tropes show it the instability of such certainties in a way that likewise lies close to ordinary consciousness; for it too calls the appearances and finite things to its aid, and from the difference among them as well as from the equal right of all to assert themselves, from the antinomy to be cognized in the finite itself, it recognizes the untruth of the same.

It can therefore be regarded as the first stage to philosophy, for the beginning of philosophy must surely be the elevation above the truth that ordinary consciousness gives, and the presentiment of a higher truth.
